key_insight: A conditional diffusion model can generate realistic, experimentally grounded spatiotemporal evolutions of turbulent flames, including unseen transition events like liftoff and reattachment.
engineering_relevance: This offers a data-driven surrogate for studying flame dynamics in data-sparse combustor settings, complementing experiments and CFD for analysis and scenario generation.
method: x-prediction flow matching for conditional diffusion
Pixel-based spatiotemporal transformer generates full space-time slabs
Transition synthesis via time-varying mixing of attached and detached denoising velocities
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that generated flames preserved key flame features and statistical consistency, especially at large scales, while errors grew for higher temporal frequencies and smaller spatial scales depending on slab duration.
watch_item: Fidelity appears to degrade at fine spatial/temporal scales, so model outputs may be less reliable for fast transients or high-resolution physics.
paper_title: Generating synthetic evolution of turbulent flames with an experimental data-based spatiotemporal diffusion model
